steps.text: Combine water, 2 tablespoons sugar, and cornstarch in a small saucepan. Cook over low heat, stirring constantly, until clear and thickened, about 2 minutes. Remove from heat.

Beat egg whites, cream of tartar, and salt in a large glass or metal bowl until foamy. Add vanilla. Gradually beat in remaining 6 tablespoons sugar until soft peaks form. Gradually beat in cornstarch mixture until stiff, glossy peaks form. Spread meringue over hot pie filling, sealing to the crust. Brown in the oven as desired.

review.reviewBody: Here are some things to know about meringue that will help you if you are unclear about some of the directions in this recipe. 1) Make sure you have completely seperated the yolk from the white... the slightest bit of yolk will break down you whites. 2) Make you your mixing bowl is 100% GREASE FREE!!! Very important! 3) Keep your eggwhites at ROOM TEMP before you beat. 4) Begin beating the egg whites slowly, increasing speed when they are frothy and beating until soft peaks just begin to form. Continue beating, slowly adding the sugar and then the cornstarch mixture. Beat the egg whites until stiff peaks form, this takes a little time. Egg whites are "STIFF" when the beaters leave ridges in the whites and they are glossy and hold a stiff peak when the beaters are lifted out. 5) It is VERY important to beat your eggwhites completely and not stop until you are ready to put on the pie. Meringue starts to deflate within 5 minutes of turning off the mixer. Hope this helps!!

I took the advice of Emily and used 1/3 c cornstarch in place of the flour since I'm gluten free. It turned out beautifully! I did have to turn up the heat when cooking the water, sugar, and cornstarch. Low temp wasn't getting the job done.
Wonderful recipe! Worked even without the cream of tartar and -more surprisingly- without an electric mixer. That's right, with just a metal bowl and a whisk (and lots of elbow grease, of course)!

Best meringue ever! And I don't like the traditional, egg and sugar meringue for several reasons: weepy, shrinks from crust, flat, dense, egg tasting.

But I made this for a coconut cream pie, and it's the best one I've ever had. Like toasted marshmallow creme. 

I followed the directions to the letter. And had no problems whatsoever. But that's because I've been baking for 20 years. The recipe is kind of vague on a couple key points. I'll include my clarifications for anyone that's interested:

Place the cornstarch and sugar into a small saucepan, BEFORE adding the water. Then add water and stir it all together before you start the heat under pan. If you add dry to liquid in a pan, you've got problems. Which may be catastrophic.
And cook it on medium heat, stirring constantly until it thickens and becomes CLEARER. It will never be transparent. Think Vaseline opaqueness. 
Take off heat and set to the side while you prep the egg white part. HOWEVER, stir the starch mix from time to time so it stays consistent and does not form skin/lumps.

Then start beating up the egg white mixture. The whites should be room temp. They fluff up better that way. You really do only need a pinch of salt. It's not for flavor, it's science to make the meringue stay firm. 

After adding everything -the starch mix can't be too hot or you'll cook the eggs- keep an eye on the texture of the meringue. If you beat it too much it will fall. Just until it's glossy with stiff

I have made this several times and it is perfect. I believe the instruction should say to cook the cornstarch mixture until it boils and not until clear. You make this mixture the same way you make cooked pudding.

I have made this Meringue several times, but there is a couple of tricks to it. The cornstarch mixture should come off the heat just before it turns to a gel. You want it to flow freely for when you are ready to use it. Today, I couldn't get the final product to peak. I slowly added a 1/2 teaspoon of cornstarch as it was beating, and it helped to stiffen the Meringue. Don't know if I just got lucky or this is a valid tip. Just know it worked for me.
EXCELLENT.. Is definitely fluffy and very creamy flavor. I added a little lemon juice right at the end of beating to add a zing. Made to top a lemon pie

This recipe is phenomenal. I doubled it and it was a little too sweet for our liking. Next time we will try reducing the sugar by one third.

Browned it for 20 minutes at 350.

The meringue is gorgeous. Makes for a very impressive pie! Thanks so much for sharing this recipe.
I finally have made a really beautiful lemon meringue pie - thank you for this wonder ful recipe, BTW, I did my cornstarch and sugar mixture in the microwave.

I made this for Easter. It was very good, and as advertised, does not weep.....a big plus. However, cooking the cornstartch syrup on low heat until it clears took over 1/2 hour. I eventually raised the heat to get it to clear. Then, when adding the syrup to the foamy egg white mixture, again it took forever for stiff peaks to form. So, while this is very good, it takes a lot longer than advertised to make.

Used 4 large eggs instead of three. Followed recipe to the T otherwise. Cornstarch syrup doesn’t get clear, but does turn opaque and quite thick. I put this on top of a banana pudding and toasted with a torch. This was absolutely delicious!! I had never made a meringue before... turned out perfect!!
The best tasting meringue I've ever made, and I've made many over 50+ years of cooking. Browns nicely, really good flavor without being overpoweringly sweet, and fluffs quickly.

Made this recipe recently to finish my lemon pie, It was worth trying this recipe because it turned out perfectly. My meringue always fails. It’s embarrassing. I’ve been cooking for 45 years. This is the first Meringue that’s turned out picture perfect and tasty.

I am not very experienced with making Meringue, however, this was an easy-to-follow recipe and set up nicely. I browned the top and made it look very pretty with toasted coconut. Let's hope the "in-laws" love it!
My cornstarch mixture did not get clear, but it still turned out beautifully!

It took me 2 weeping pies to give this a try. Within 15 minutes of it coming out of the stove 3/4 of the meringue has not only weeped a river, it shrank. I have had trouble with a little weeping but never shrinking. Nasty ..
Finally, I found a good recipe for meringue! I have been trying diferente recipes and this one wins, by far! I’m only wondering if it’s safe to eat without baking it.
Accurate, and so good!
!!! EASY AS PIE !!! I used whole vanilla wafers as the crust for banana cream pie and baked it in 400-degree over for 7 min. to lightly brown meringue.
Excellent recipe! Turned out beautiful & delicious! The best meringue ever! Thank you for sharing! Laurie
